title: The Royal Physician's Cure for Greed (KN)
summary: A miserly courtier complains of a mysterious ailment that makes him miserable despite wealth. Birbal prescribes the medicine of generosity. [KN]
full_text:
A fabulously wealthy courtier named Seth Ramdas visited the royal court physician, complaining of a severe, chronic illness: 'Hakimji, I cannot sleep, my chest burns with anxiety, food tastes like ashes in my mouth, and I feel a crushing weight upon my heart day and night! I have taken gold tonics, saffron syrups, and pearl powders, yet my misery only increases! Cure me!'

The court physician examined the merchant's pulse, looked at his tongue, and shook his head: 'Sethji, your physical body is in perfect health. Your illness is an affliction of the spirit, and only Raja Birbal knows the remedy for such a disease.'

The merchant went to Birbal's house, begging for a cure.

Birbal looked at the miserable millionaire and asked: 'Sethji, how many houses do you own in Agra?'

'Twelve palaces, my lord.'

'How many sacks of gold lie in your cellar?'

'Fifty heavy iron chests.'

'And how many copper coins did you give to the starving orphan children outside your gate this morning?'

The merchant blinked in confusion: 'None! Why should I give away my hard-earned money to street beggars?'

Birbal smiled with gentle pity, stood up, and wrote a royal prescription on a slip of parchment:

'Here is your medicine, Seth Ramdas. It requires neither gold powder nor bitter herbs:

'Tomorrow morning, take two heavy bags of silver coins from your cellar. Walk on foot through the poorest slums of Agra.

'Find ten widowed mothers who have no bread for their children, and pay their food for a year.

'Find twenty crippled beggars, and buy them warm woolen blankets.

'Find five sick laborers, and pay the physician for their medicines.

'Do this for three consecutive mornings, and your burning chest will cool, your sleep will become sweet as honey, and food will taste delicious once again!'

The merchant was reluctant, but desperate to cure his agonizing misery, he obeyed the prescription.

Three days later, Ramdas ran into Akbar's durbar, his face radiant with joyful tears, falling at Birbal's feet:

'A miracle, Raja Birbal! The moment I wiped the tears from those starving children and saw them smile, the crushing stone on my chest dissolved! I slept like an infant last night for the first time in twenty years!'

Birbal smiled at Emperor Akbar: 'Greed is a poison that suffocates the human heart in its own hoard. Generosity is the only medicine that opens the windows of the soul to the fresh air of heaven.'

Akbar commended Birbal for healing the merchant's soul with the medicine of compassion.
